I am reminded of press space so I will just mention one or two matters of interest. Firstly—Fred Rickards—a stalwart. His performances over long distance walks are written elsewhere but he must be mentioned for his pluck.

From 1924 to 1939, a period of 16 years, the race was won eight times by Fred Rickards and four times by Fred Bentley. Now, after trying for 21 years, our vice-captain, Jack Bidgood, has added his name to the list of Belgrave successes, beating Tom Kent, the winner for the past three years, over the last mile.
Much could be written of Tommy Green’s magnificent performances and those of Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and others, but space does not permit.

Fred Rickards sends best wishes to all and says he hopes to be on the road again soon. In the Civil Service Championships, Jack Brown was second in the 1 mile and Charlie Smart gained a similar position in the 3 miles event.

…), Hugh McGreechan (6th), Jack Stirling Wakely (10th), and Harry Shields (11th), scored an easy win for us; and veteran Fred Rickards—one of the greatest walkers and finest sportsmen ever—was our fifth man to finish in a position that would still have enabled us to win even if one of our first four…

…t and most popular distance walkers, namely, Colin Sutton, just returned from Australia looking very brown and fit, and Fred Rickards, who informed us he was going to make a comeback, not looking quite so brown, but fitter and, if possible, more chirpy than ever.…
Fred Rickards, an almost legendary figure, staged a come-back and, despite a bad time around 20 miles, walked so well that he was fifth Belgrave to finish.
Fred Rickards was then our second man in 21st position with George Checkley, not looking too happy, and Harry Shields following close behind.

Roberts, Jack Rutland, George Checkley, Fred Rickards and Frank Thomson. Frank is particularly mentioned for his tremendous effort in regaling the walkers from first to last with Horlicks and sponging, and it was truly amazing to see such vitality from one of his age.

Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and Hugh have all won on three successive occasions and Hugh looked all set for it this year. However that very improved young walker, McFarlane of the Poly, who incidentally seems to spend more time with us than his own club, beat Mc.to it and so the battle for this honour still goes on.

Names like Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley, and Jack Bidgood remind us of the past years, but now it would seem that George Checkley and Hugh McGreechan have taken on the task of keeping a Belgrave name on the trophy.
